text:
A: Alright, how's it going?
B: Hiya, hello. Yeah, good thanks. Can you hear me okay?
A: Loud and clear. I'm Zain, Bolton.
B: I'm Gemma. I'm in Long Eaton, which is, erm, between Derby and Nottingham, sort of.
A: Ah, nice. Been past it on the M1, I think. What do you do?
B: I work in a hospital pharmacy in Nottingham. I'm a pharmacy technician, so not a pharmacist, I'm just a tech. I do the medicines on two of the wards, checking what people are on when they come in, that kind of thing.
A: Just a tech, behave. That sounds proper important.
B: Well, it's sort of my job to catch it if something's wrong on a prescription. So I suppose it is, yeah. What about you?
A: Sparky. Electrician, domestic and commercial, for a firm in Manchester. Rewires, consumer units, EV chargers, that's the big one now. I were out at half six this morning in Horwich. Bloke's had three people round about a tripping fault and nobody could find it. Took me about forty minutes. Water in an outside socket. He were made up.
B: Oh, my husband's an electrician!
A: No way. Who's he with?
B: Just a small local firm. Rob. He'd love you, he's always moaning that people don't check outside sockets.
A: See, he knows. Tell him from me, he's right.
B: I will. He'll be chuffed.
A: I'm going on my own in a couple of years, hopefully. Get a van with my name on it, do EV chargers and solar. That's where the money is, if you ask me.
B: That's brilliant. Rob's always talking about going self-employed but he never does. He worries about the paperwork, the tax and the insurance and everything.
A: Yeah, that's... that's the bit, to be fair. I'll get someone for that.
B: Ha, sensible.
A: Did you do that puzzle thing at the start?
B: Oh, I did, and I sort of overthought it. I kept going back and checking. Which is my job, really, but you can't do that in a timed thing, if that makes sense?
A: Mate, I just went for it. Probably got half of it wrong.
B: Probably the better way, honestly.
A: You got a dog? I'm sure I saw a dog in your photo.
B: Yes! That's Biscuit. She's a greyhound, a rescue. She's twelve, sorry, thirteen in March. She's on the sofa behind me now, hiding because she's terrified of the hoover. We walk along the canal every day, and I do parkrun on a Saturday.
A: Parkrun, fair play. I do five-a-side on Wednesdays. One of the lads never passes, does my head in.
B: There's always one.
A: Every time. What do you do for tea after a shift then, are you a cook?
B: Batch cook, mostly. Chilli, bolognese, a chicken casserole, all in labelled tubs in the freezer. I'm trying to do more veggie, but Rob's suspicious of lentils.
A: Ha, tell him daal. My mum's daal would convert anyone. She still sends me home with tubs every Sunday.
B: That's lovely. My mum does the same with the Sunday dinner leftovers.
A: Mums, man. Best people.
B: They are. Oh, I think we're nearly out of time.
